senses.gloss:
Aulāna is a word occurring in a single passage of the Rigveda, where it may possibly be a patronymic of śaṃtanu as a ‘descendant of ula.’ Ludwig, however, conjectures that the reading should be ‘Kaulāna.’ Sieg regards aulāna as a later descendant of śaṃtanu, who utilized the story of Devāpi's rain-making as an introduction to his rain hymn.
Foot notes x. 98, 11.
Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 166.
Die Sagenstoffe des ṛgveda, 141.
Cf. Sāyaṇa on Rv. x, 98, 11; kuru kula-jātaḥ Śāṃtaṇavaḥ, ‘a descendant of śaṃtanu, born in the family of the Kurus
